attacks.claim: The cost math mislabels a daily figure as monthly. 38M lines/day x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens per day, which is ~$1,140/day, or ~$34k/month. That is about 23x the $1,500 budget, and a 61M-line peak day costs ~$1,830 in input alone. The plan is not viable as designed, and it has no sampling, filtering, or spend cap.
attacks.evidence: "Input: 38M lines x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens -> ~$1,140" and "Estimated total: ~$1,150/month, within the $1,500 budget."

attacks.claim: Every application log line is forwarded to the LLM, so input cost and queue load grow linearly with log volume. A 10x log growth or an incident-time error storm would multiply spend and queue backlog with no dedup, sampling, or per-service cap. Pre-aggregating by signature before the LLM is the obvious design, and it is absent.
attacks.evidence: "forwards every application log line to the summarizer queue"

attacks.claim: The staffing math ignores the stated 50% on-call/interrupt load. Two engineers have about 6 eng-weeks of real capacity in 6 calendar weeks, not 12, so the schedule is about 2x optimistic (~12 weeks). The plan also assigns both engineers full-time, leaving nobody for incident coverage.
attacks.evidence: "both platform engineers full-time for 6 weeks (2 x 6 = 12 eng-weeks)" vs. context "on-call/interrupt work averages 50% of their time"

attacks.claim: The redaction stage masks only emails, tokens, card numbers, and IPs, and it was audited for the retention policy, not for sending data to a third-party processor. Customer names, tenant IDs, and free-text payloads in logs may still reach the external LLM. The DPA and zero-retention setting mitigate this, but no re-audit for this use is planned.
attacks.evidence: "already masks emails, tokens, card numbers and IPs for our log retention policy (audited in Q1)"

attacks.claim: The plan has no failure handling for LLM outages, rate limits, or queue backlog. It does not say what the on-call engineer sees when summaries are stale or missing. It also does not address prompt injection from log content, or misleading summaries posted into PagerDuty.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retry/timeout/backpressure, staleness indicator, and injection handling

attacks.claim: With 40 incidents, a launch gate of <=5% misleading means at most 2 misleading summaries, so the sample is statistically weak. The eval is also graded by a single reviewer type, and the plan does not say how MTTR improvement will be measured against the baseline.
